title: Movement
canon: New York City, September through November 2012, across the collegiate fall term and the mayoral election. Seven gifted international students at a Columbia-like university in upper Manhattan are secretly recruited into the Lab for International Specialists and trained through covert missions by the Professor, who serves the Unknown Global Consortium. While the seven believe they are defending Mayor Grace Camarda's re-election against UGC-backed billionaire Ben Gilman, every mission secretly bends the race the consortium's way.
look: Marco's canon names the look outright: the Bourne series — kinetic handheld camera, staccato energy, stark contrast, realism. 2012 New York in the fall, shot as if by a documentary crew embedded with the students: available light only, cold institutional daylight, sodium and fluorescent city night, green banker's lamps in the library. Nothing stylized or futuristic; the conspiracy hides inside an ordinary, believable city. Every frame full-bleed, no letterbox.
note: Period, place, and look come straight from movement-canon.md (the ~20k-word treatment: 'September 2012: New York City', campus 'modeled after Columbia perhaps', 'I really like the style of the Bourne series... stark contrast, the realism') and the ruled 00f-season-one-synopsis.md (fall term through election night). Shots chosen: the recruitment quad walk, the library at 3am, the seven-empty-jackets hero (keeping the approved concept from 06-movement-01-hero.jpg), the Lower East Side electronics-store HQ front (canon's most ownable location, replacing the sci-fi server-room render), City Hall on election night (anchored to the real building via city-hall.jpg), and the rooftop dawn poster frame. Failures these prompts fix: prior renders drew a collegiate-gothic Princeton campus instead of Columbia's Beaux-Arts classical idiom, pasted Philadelphia City Hall into the skyline (movement_hero_1.jpeg), and shipped pillarbox black bars (02, 08, movement-quad). CAST-CONTINUITY WARNING: canon contains no physical descriptions of the seven; the faces in 01-seven-students-fog.png are the only de facto cast and are used as the cast/wardrobe ref wherever the seven appear with visible faces — Marco should rule whether those seven faces become canonical before wide generation. — 2026-07-16 Story-Law pass: appended six story shots (bomb-hunt-lecture-hall, donor-stakeout, aid-crate-weapons, wounded-at-the-back-door, reporter-corkboard, gilman-deputy-screens) mined from the ruled 00f-season-one-synopsis.md — EP101 bomb test, EP103 surveillance + Kotone's analog save, EP105 weapons-moved-not-stopped, EP107 the Reporter's near-exposure, EP108 the cost, EP110 the inverted win. Each frame shows what is happening and what is at stake per STORY-LAW.md; refs carry cast/wardrobe only. Existing six shots untouched. PERIOD FLAG: the synopsis ⚑ answers say 'Contemporary' for the period while this spec and all prior stills are locked to fall 2012 — Marco should reconcile before wide generation.

stills.notes: Ref carries the de facto faces and wardrobe of the seven only. Prompt owns the campus: fixes the gothic-Princeton drift by describing Columbia's Beaux-Arts classical idiom, and owns the fog-dawn light.
stills.prompt: The campus of a great Ivy League university in Morningside Heights, upper Manhattan, September 2012, seven in the morning on the first day of the fall term. A long granite walk runs between brick-and-limestone Beaux-Arts halls toward a domed neoclassical library at the head of a broad flight of steps, everything softened by low fog. Seven international students in their early twenties — jackets, backpacks, jeans — walk toward camera down the centre of the walk, spread loosely, not yet a team, each glancing at the others as if recognizing something. The only light is the flat grey dawn skylight diffused through the fog, plus the last of the cast-iron path lamps still burning weak and orange down the walk; no sun, no hard shadows, faces lit soft and even by the sky. Handheld wide frame at eye level, 35mm film still, stark contrast, natural grain, documentary realism. Full-bleed frame, no letterbox, no black bars. No text, no watermark.

stills.notes: No recurring face needs to hold — the figure reads as any of the seven deep in the Professor's first puzzle. Prompt owns the single-practical light logic and kills the pillarbox bars that ruined 02-library-3am.png.
stills.prompt: Interior of the main reading room of a university library in upper Manhattan, New York, three in the morning, October 2012. A vast McKim-style hall with coffered ceiling and tall arched windows, every window fogged with condensation and reading almost black, holding only a faint cold blue wash of city glow from outside. Hundreds of empty oak chairs and long tables recede into darkness. At one table a single student in his early twenties sits hunched over spread papers and notebooks, and the only warm light in the frame is the one green-shaded banker's lamp burning in front of him, throwing a hot pool on the tabletop and underlighting his face; every other lamp down the tables is dark. Deep shadow, high contrast, the practical highlight blooming slightly. Wide symmetrical composition down the length of the table, 35mm film still, natural grain, cinematic realism. Full-bleed frame, no letterbox, no black bars. No text, no watermark.

stills.notes: Keeps the approved hero concept. Ref carries wardrobe only — the seven distinct jackets that stand in for the seven characters (trench, navy overcoat, denim, black puffer, grey tweed, olive parka, brown leather). Prompt owns the room and the two-source light logic.
stills.prompt: Interior of the same great university reading room in upper Manhattan, New York, autumn 2012, an hour before dawn. A long oak table in the empty hall, and draped over the backs of seven chairs along one side hang seven very different jackets — a beige trench coat, a navy wool overcoat, a faded denim jacket, a black down puffer, a grey tweed blazer, an olive military parka, a brown leather jacket — as if seven people were just here and will return, though the room is deserted. Two sources of light only: the cold blue pre-dawn glow seeping through the tall arched windows on the left, hazy in the air, and one green-shaded banker's lamp lit at the middle of the table, throwing a single warm pool across the wood. All other lamps down the hall are dark. Symmetrical frontal composition, deep shadow, high contrast, 35mm film still, natural grain, cinematic. Full-bleed frame, no letterbox, no black bars. No text, no watermark.

stills.notes: Canon's most ownable location — the Lower East Side electronics store that fronts the Movement's real HQ — replacing the sci-fi server-room render that broke 2012 realism. Prompt owns storefront geography and the three-source night light.
stills.prompt: A narrow electronics store on a tenement block of the Lower East Side, New York, a wet November night in 2012. Cramped storefront under a fire escape, its window stacked with boxed video game consoles, cheap flat-screen TVs all playing, tangles of phone accessories, handwritten price stickers. A young woman in her early twenties with a backpack pauses at the recessed side door beside the shop, keying a code, glancing up the empty street. Three light sources only: the dead sodium-orange streetlamp glow down the block, the shifting blue-white flicker of the stacked television screens spilling across the wet sidewalk, and a bare fluorescent tube burning inside the shop. Reflections doubling everything in the wet asphalt. Handheld frame from across the street, slight long-lens compression, 35mm film still, stark contrast, natural grain, surveillance-adjacent realism. Full-bleed frame, no letterbox, no black bars. No text, no watermark.

stills.notes: Ref holds the real New York City Hall facade so the model does not substitute Philadelphia City Hall (the movement_hero_1.jpeg failure). Prompt owns the election-night crowd and broadcast light.
stills.prompt: New York City Hall, lower Manhattan, election night, November 2012, in light rain. The white Federal-style hall with its cupola floodlit against the dark, the Municipal Building tower looming behind through drizzle. On the plaza before the steps a press scrum and campaign crowd under umbrellas: news vans, TV crews, supporters with rain-slick coats. The light comes only from what is there — the floodlights washing the facade, the hard white camera-mounted lights and HMI panels of the broadcast crews raking across faces, red-and-blue police light bars strobing at the barricades, and all of it smeared in reflections across the wet paving. No daylight anywhere. Handheld long-lens frame from inside the crowd, heads and shoulders breaking the foreground, 35mm film still, stark contrast, natural grain, news-footage realism. Full-bleed frame, no letterbox, no black bars. No text, no watermark.

stills.notes: The poster frame. Figures stay silhouettes so no cast ref is needed. Prompt names the real skyline geography and bans the pillarbox bars that shipped on 08-rooftop-dawn.png.
stills.prompt: The tar rooftop of a prewar apartment building in upper Manhattan, New York, dawn in late autumn 2012. Seven young figures stand in silhouette along the parapet, spread in a loose line, looking south toward the skyline where the Empire State Building rises through golden haze, midtown behind it, the city below still sunk in blue shadow. The only light is the low sun just clearing the East Side, burning through morning haze — it rim-lights the seven from behind and flares softly across the wet roof tar and parapet stone; no artificial light anywhere, windows of the city still dark. Wide anamorphic composition from behind and slightly above the group, 35mm film still, heavy natural grain, cinematic. Full-bleed frame, no letterbox, no black bars. No text, no watermark.

stills.prompt: A steep-raked lecture hall in a Beaux-Arts university building in Morningside Heights, upper Manhattan, September 2012, late on the first afternoon of the fall term. Seven international students in their early twenties — strangers who met an hour ago — are tearing the empty hall apart mid-search: one prying a floor-level ventilation grille open with a chair leg, two crawling the rows checking under fold-down seats, one halfway up the aisle holding a creased handwritten note to the window light, and at the lectern one young man halting a young woman with a flat palm an inch before she touches the wired junction box inside an opened access panel, exposed cabling caught in her flashlight beam. Backpacks dumped in the aisle, a round institutional wall clock above the blackboard. The only light is the cold grey institutional daylight through the tall windows and the green-white buzz of the overhead fluorescents, plus that one small handheld flashlight beam; nothing else. Handheld frame from the top of the raked seating, slightly tilted, urgent, 35mm film still, stark contrast, natural grain, documentary realism. Full-bleed frame, no letterbox, no black bars. No text, no watermark.

stills.notes: EP103, the first field mission that works — surveilling a Gilman donor — plus Marco's ruled anti-tech beat: Kotone's paper notebook working while the camera's screen is dead. The side mirror carries the counter-stake: the watchers are being watched. Ref carries faces/wardrobe only.
stills.prompt: Inside a parked older grey sedan on a brownstone block of the Upper East Side, New York, October 2012, near midnight. Two of the seven students work the car: a young man in the driver's seat braces a long telephoto lens on the wheel, aimed across the street at the lit doorway of a townhouse where a silver-haired man in a topcoat hands a slim briefcase down to a waiting driver; in the back seat a young Japanese woman writes licence plates longhand in a paper notebook, because the digital camera lying between the seats is dead, its screen black. Sharp in the driver's side mirror: the silhouette of a second parked car down the block, two heads inside, facing them. Light only from what is there — the amber sodium streetlamps down the row, the warm spill of the townhouse doorway lantern across the sidewalk, a faint dashboard glow; no screens alive anywhere. Shot from the back seat over their shoulders through the windshield, handheld, long-lens compression on the doorway, 35mm film still, stark contrast, natural grain, surveillance realism. Full-bleed frame, no letterbox, no black bars. No text, no watermark.

Appolonia (the weapons expert — she alone knows exactly what she is looking at) opens a relief crate and finds rifles; the manifest and the glance back at the gate put the lie and the danger in the same frame. stills.prompt: Interior of a brick warehouse loading bay in Red Hook, Brooklyn, New York, a cold October night in 2012, the roll gate half open to the wet street. A young Basque woman in her early twenties stands over a wooden shipping crate she has just crowbarred open — the lid at her feet stencilled with a red cross and relief markings rendered soft and unreadable — and inside, packed in grease paper and straw, lie rows of military rifles. She holds the crowbar loose at her side and stares at them, jaw set, because she alone knows exactly what she is looking at. Two other students flank her, one gripping a paper manifest, one already looking back over his shoulder at the gate. Identical crates stacked on pallets recede behind them. Light only as found: one caged work bulb hanging low over the open crate throwing hard downlight, the sodium orange of the street washing in under the half-open gate, the cold spill of a forklift's headlamps left burning at the frame edge. Handheld frame at chest height, close enough to read the rifles and her face, 35mm film still, stark contrast, natural grain, documentary realism. Full-bleed frame, no letterbox, no black bars. No text, no watermark.

stills.notes: EP108, the cost — a mission goes wrong and one of the seven is hurt. Reuses the electronics-store-hq storefront and its exact three-source night light so the location cuts together across stills. Ref carries faces/wardrobe only.
stills.prompt: The recessed side door beside a narrow electronics store on a tenement block of the Lower East Side, New York, a wet November night in 2012. Two students in their early twenties half-carry a third between them — his arms over their shoulders, feet dragging, one trouser leg dark and wet with blood, jaw clenched — while a fourth, a young woman, holds the steel door open with her back and scans up the empty street, her free hand waving them in. The storefront's stacked televisions flicker through the window beside them. Three light sources only: the dead sodium-orange streetlamp glow down the block, the shifting blue-white flicker of the television screens spilling across the wet sidewalk and across the wounded boy's face, and the bare fluorescent tube burning in the stairwell behind the open door. A broken line of blood drops on the wet pavement behind them. Handheld frame from across the narrow street, slightly low, rushed, 35mm film still, stark contrast, natural grain, documentary realism. Full-bleed frame, no letterbox, no black bars. No text, no watermark.

stills.notes: EP107, the exposure risk — the Reporter has nearly proven the Movement is real, and one of the seven finds his own face pinned on the wall. Ref carries the seven faces both for the intruder and for the pinned surveillance photos. Per Marco's ruling the Janitor stays non-lethal, so the exposure beat belongs to the students themselves.
stills.prompt: A cluttered newsroom office in an old downtown Manhattan building, November 2012, long after midnight, venetian-blind stripes of city glow across the walls. A young American man in his early twenties stands frozen before a corkboard that fills the wall: pinned surveillance photographs of seven young students — his own face at the center — linked by taut red string to photographs of a Lower East Side storefront, a university gate, and New York City Hall, every scrap of writing on the board reduced to illegible scrawl. His small flashlight beam is the hot point of the frame, pinned on his own photograph, and his other hand is already reaching up to unpin it. Light only as found: the narrow flashlight beam, the cold blue city glow bleeding through the blinds, and one green-shaded desk lamp left burning across the room. Handheld frame from behind his shoulder, the board looming over him, 35mm film still, stark contrast, natural grain, documentary realism. Full-bleed frame, no letterbox, no black bars. No text, no watermark.

stills.notes: EP110, the price — Camarda wins and the storefront televisions show the billionaire raised at her side as deputy. A different beat from city-hall-election-night (the scrum outside the hall): this is the seven, fresh from their own victory party, reading the inversion in the glass. Ref carries faces/wardrobe only.
stills.prompt: The lit window of a narrow electronics store on a tenement block of the Lower East Side, New York, election night, November 2012, near midnight, the rain just stopped. Every stacked television in the window plays the same live news feed: on a flag-dressed victory stage a triumphant woman mayor in her sixties raises the arm of the tall silver-haired billionaire standing at her side while confetti falls, every chyron and graphic soft and unreadable. On the wet sidewalk in front of the glass stand the seven students, just come from a victory party — a campaign button on one lapel, a strand of confetti still on a shoulder, one still holding a small paper flag — and the celebration is dying on their faces as they watch. Light only as found: the blue-white flicker of the screens on their faces, the dead sodium-orange streetlamp down the block, and both smeared in reflections across the wet pavement. Handheld frame from along the storefront glass, the wall of screens on one side and the seven's faces on the other, 35mm film still, stark contrast, natural grain, documentary realism. Full-bleed frame, no letterbox, no black bars. No text, no watermark.
